text.tspan: Awaiting in a loop is a queue. Promise.all is a starting gun for tasks that do not depend on each other.
await one at a time: 3 seconds
start them all, then await: 1 second
First to SETTLE wins, even if
Only fan out when the tasks are INDEPENDENT. If step B needs step A's result, awaiting in sequence is not a bug; it is
the requirement. And Promise.all does not create threads: the waiting overlaps, the JavaScript still runs on one thread.
